MUNSHI MURDER FOLLOW

By: Latashia Naidoo | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A year after renowned anaesthesiologist Dr Abdulhay Munshi was gunned down, his death continues to raise questions among his family and colleagues.

Unique Selling Point:
The shocking daytime murder of a prominent medical specialist sent ripples through the SA medical fraternity last year. And medical practitioners around the country now claim to be living in fear for their own lives.

Summary:
More than a year after Johannesburg anaesthesiologist, Dr Abdulhay Munshi was gunned down in broad daylight in Orange Grove, his family - and the medical fraternity - are still searching for answers.

At the time of the killing, a Joburg father who took Munshi and paediatric surgeon Professor Peter Beale to court over the death of his 10-year-old son, Zayyaan Sayed during an operation, denied having a hand in the murder.
Mohammadh and Zaheena Sayed had laid charges against Drs Beale and Munshi after the death of their 10-year-old son Zayyaan at the Park Lane Clinic.

The Medical Protection Society and the HPCSA have now called for more proactive police investigations into the murder, saying it’s struck fear among surgeons in the province that they too could fall victim to alleged “vigilantism”.
The medical fraternity had previously speculated that the culpable homicide case related to the death of Zayyaan and Munshi's shooting could be linked.
Munshi’s family, too, are still demanding answers - and closure.
They want to know how a prominent doctor’s death has fallen on the wayside of police investigations.

*** A look at the status of the investigation a year on, as well as inferences to possible mob involvement, and the psychological effect the murder has had on colleagues within the medical industry.

Press Release:


Who’s Next?
In September last year, the sound of six shots, fired in quick succession, rang out on a busy workday afternoon in Orange Grove, Johannesburg: a prominent medical specialist senselessly gunned down in broad daylight. Now, more than a year later and despite public outrage, the investigation into his murder has stalled. With no leads and no witnesses, his killers remain at large and the medical fraternity is left asking, “who could be next”?
Producer: Latashia Naidoo | Presenter: Bongani Bingwa 

Script:


MUNSHI MURDER DRAFT SCRIPT
OPENING SEQUENCE:
DRAMATISATION: SIX SHOTS FIRED, POLICE SIRENS, BLOOD, ‘September 16, 2020, 3:50pm
VO:
A deadly and brazen shooting in the middle of a busy Johannesburg suburb. A prominent doctor, gunned down at point blank range.
DAN: Fade the eyewitness news report .. fade audio at the end – let audio overlap with the first line.
Vo:
It was a crime that struck fear into the hearts of an entire medical community.
But more than a year after Dr Abdulhay Munshi was allegedly assassinated, his killers remain at large.
LINK 1: CANON CAM 1 – A104C356_21112262
Dr Munshi was coming up to this busy intersection in Orange Grove. He was rear-ended and he got out of his car to try and check the damage. And that’s when his assailants shot him six times, in broad daylight, on a Wednesday afternoon.
VIZ: CRIME SCENE TAPE, POLICE SIRENS, ETC (CAN WE USE MORE OF THE DRONE FOOTAGE HERE, PLEASE)
VO:
Was this a random attack? Or an assassination carried out by hired guns? If it was an assassination, there may have been some specific reasons as to why.
VO:
Among the medical community and on social media, speculations have run rampant.

TWEET 1, 2
VO: One doctor tweeted that Dr Munshi was shot and killed in what appeared to be revenge for a poor patient outcome.
While another suggested that the medical fraternity was now coming face to face with “The seedy underbelly of the criminal world.”
VO:
Whatever the motives, no one knows for sure just why Dr Munshi become the target of gun-wielding assailants on a seemingly ordinary afternoon.
And the reason no one knows is because there have been no arrests for his murder.
VIZ: HEADLINES - Paediatric surgeon and anaesthetist accused of culpable homicide appear in court (702.co.za)
Doctors arrested after death of Johannesburg boy, post-surgery, get bail (timeslive.co.za)
VO:
Here’s what we do know:
At the time of his murder, Dr Munshi was the co-accused in a culpable homicide case with paediatric surgeon, Professor Peter Beale – relating to the death of a 10-year-old boy at the Netcare Park Lane Hospital in October 2019.
The tragedy sparked huge a outcry, and both doctors were charged for medical negligence.
VIZ: TIMES HEADLINE
VO:
What we don’t know for certain is whether there was a connection between that death and Dr Munshi’s, and that’s what continues to make people jittery.
Professor Beale went into hiding shortly after his co-accused’s murder – and has not been seen in public since.
NATALIE: A104C381_211123C1 - 11:57 - 12:34
“We have asked, and we would like to continue to ask, for the police services to investigate this case and give feedback to the community as to what caused Dr Munshi’s murder. It’s not the only time that a healthcare worker has been attacked, and healthcare workers are scared. They’re scared because they are vulnerable. And they’re scared because they don’t know if their job will bring them ‘harm’.”
VO:
Natalie Zimmelman is the CEO of the South African Society of Anaesthesiologists(SASA).
VIZ: STATEMENTS
VIZ: https://www.medicalprotection.org/southafrica/casebook-and-resources/news/news-article/2020/09/17/mps-statement-on-death-of-dr-abdulhay-munshi
News (netcarehospitals.co.za)
Minister Zweli Mkhize on passing of Dr Abdulhay Munshi | South African Government (www.gov.za)
VO:
Zimmelman says the tragedy has also shone a spotlight on the handling of medico-legal issues in the country. At the centre of the culpable homicide controversy is the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA), the regulatory body that ensures healthcare professionals practice ethically.
NATALIE: A104C381_211123C1 - 10:00 - 10:23
“We would’ve liked to have seen the HPCSA act faster, act more effectively, and to have started an inquiry that could give the doctors, the family, the process, answers that it was seeking. But instead, it went straight to prosecution. And the act of starting that prosecution then suspends any inquiry that could’ve happened.””
VIZ: USE EMAIL AS WELL AS SCREENSHOT
VO:
The HPCSA failed to respond to questions we put forward to them regarding the allegations made by SASA and other medical groups in the handling of the internal investigations.
VIDEO OF BEALE LEAVING: (1) Iavan Pijoos on Twitter: "Paediatric surgeon Dr Peter Beale leaving the Johannesburg Magistrate’s Court after being granted bail of R10,000. @TimesLIVE https://t.co/FWGSO8Pl98" / Twitter
VO:
In January 2021, Professor Beale was formally charged with murder and fraud, and the matter is ongoing. All charges against Dr Munshi have since been dropped.
LINK 3: CANON LAST 2 LINKS – A106C424_21112340
“Who was Dr Munshi? Speak to anyone who worked closely with him, and they’re full of praise. But the consequence of his unsolved murder means that many of them aren’t willing to come forward and speak on the record. We tried and tried and tried – and were met with a wall of silence.”
VO:
Worryingly, it’s the people who have been tasked with bringing his killers to book whose silence in this story has been most deafening.
While the lawlessness speaks for itself, both the South African Police Service and the National Prosecuting Authority have revealed very little information about the status of this high profile murder – 15 months later.
All they’ve said is that investigations are ongoing.
It’s only heightened fears as to “why” justice has yet to prevail for a man described by so many as a ‘gentle giant” and a “consummate professional”.
VIZ: SUPERIMPOSE MUNSHI SMILING PIC ON SCREEN WITH QUOTES – “A very gentle, very quiet man”, “Unbelievably respected”, “Dedicated frontline worker”, “A mentor to so many”, “tremendously experienced”, “Kind beyond measure”
ADRIAN WEBB: ADRIAN: CANON – A104C3962 _211123MR
VO:
Anaesthetist Dr Adrian Webb’s relationship with the late Dr Munshi spanned 25 years. The pair trained together as specialists in the mid-90’s, and worked closely together in private practice for decades.
Dr Webb is one of just a handful of former colleagues of Dr Munshi’s who were willing to be interviewed about his death on-camera.
ADRIAN: 07:56 “I was utterly shocked. I was really – I still haven’t got over the way that it happened, and the unfairness of the whole situation. I was absolutely devastated. He was a major loss to our community, and he was a personal friend too.”
VIZ: WARRANT OF ARREST, TWEET VIDEO – LEAVING TH JOBURG MAG COURT 17 DEC 2019: Iavan Pijoos on Twitter: "Anaesthetist Dr Abdulhay Munshi leaving the Johannesburg Magistrate’s Court after being granted bail of R10,000. @TimesLIVE https://t.co/At7RcqaM2m" / Twitter
VO:
According to Dr Webb, the culpable homicide charge affected Dr Munshi both professionally and personally.
And those feelings were amplified by the constant media scrutiny.
BONGANI: 00001 - 00:06:39 “I’m trying to get a sense of how difficult it must be to put your best foot forward, to want the best outcomes, and when things go wrong – instead of a lesson coming out of the situation, there’s a sense of wanting to punish the doctor. It must be difficult.”
ADRIAN: 06:58
“Extremely difficult. We’re not able to function under those circumstances. It would become very, very difficult to function where punishment is a sort of threat hanging over you all the time.”
VIZ: PLEASE USE SOME OF THIS FOOTAGE:
Showing support for Dr Abdulhay Munshi who was as gunned down. #DrMunshi # #JusticeforAbdulhay - YouTube
VO:
Some former colleagues have alleged that Dr Munshi told them he was being followed, and had even received anonymous death threats in the weeks leading up to his murder. But that the police ignored his fears – until it was too late.
VIZ: COURT 2 PIC.
LINK 4: CANON LAST 2 LINKS – A106C426_21112359
“To be a top specialist in medicine takes years of training, dedication and discipline. These are the best of the best and they hold themselves and their colleagues to the highest professional standards. And of course, things can go wrong.
VIZ: CHANGE.ORG PETITION Petition · #dropitandwait SA Doctor’s profession & patient care under threat. · Change.org
VIZ: HEADLINE 1, PLEASE HIGHLIGHT THE NUMBER OF SIGNATURES ON PETITION
VO:
It’s part of the reason why Durban-based orthopaedic surgeon, Dr Rinesh Chetty, launched a change.org petition in 2020, calling for the charges against Drs Munshi and Beale to be dropped.
VO:
Dr Chetty suggests that Dr Munshi’s murder has created a climate of trepidation for medical staff to now operate within.
RINESH: ZOOM: 20:20 - 20:45
“Because of the rising medical negligence, because of the easiness of the legal community to actually litigate, this case just amplifies and catalyses that. It has already changed the way in which doctors work; it has already changed our consent forms; it has already changed a lot of the way in which we practice medicine.
BONGANI: 2ND CAMERA - 00004 -
00:22:00 “Do doctors have enough protection, or do you look at this case and think it could be you, it could be doctors you know?”
RINESH: ZOOM: 21:42 - 21:51
“Every doctor feels the exact same way I do. Whether they want to say it out loud or not, there’s a lot of fear. I think everyone lives in fear in South Africa these days, based on the type of retribution that’s occurring.”
LINK 2: CANON CAM 1 – A104C373_2111225H
“‘First, do no harm’. That’s the sacred oath that underpins the work that all doctors do. But when things go wrong, they can be held criminally liable – for mistakes many say, leave them traumatized.”
VIZ: JOINT LETTER TO MINISTER
VO:
Earlier this month, various medical bodies petitioned the justice ministry for a review on the law on culpable homicide.
In its current form, doctors may be jailed for healthcare-related deaths – even though fatalities are sometimes unavoidable.
VO:
In recent years, dozens of healthcare workers have fallen victim to attacks by patients and others. Some doctors, like John Moche, Michael Aluko, Shongile Pretty Nkhwashu, and Oupa Chuene – have even lost their lives to murder.
While the motives for their killings may have been different none of their deaths were related to medical negligence cases.
And unlike Dr Munshi’s case, their killers have all been brought to book.
STATS: GRAPHIC: (ALL DRS PICS WITH NAMES IN DRIVE)
Dr John Moche - gunned down in Johannesburg - 2012
Dr Michael Aluko - stabbed to death in Khayelitsha - 2014
Dr Shongile Pretty Nkhwashu - murdered in Limpopo - January 2020
Dr Oupa Chuene - bludgeoned to death in Midrand - April 2021
PERCY MILLER – WETRANSFER DOWNLOAD 00007
00:15:56 “There are lots of crazy people who could’ve grabbed a weapon and done this. But if people start killing doctors, then you’ve got an open season… So it’s important that this thing is brought to justice, to make people think twice.”
VO:
For decades, neurosurgeon Percy Miller had worked side-by-side with Dr Munshi on dozens of successful procedures.
In March this year, Dr Miller wrote to Police Minister Bheki Cele, imploring him to prioritize the murder investigation – but like so many others in this story, was met with silence. He’s convinced that his friend and colleague’s death was a hit.
PERCY: 00:12:33 “In the beginning there was anger. Now, because there was a hit, however this hit happened – there’s fear. People are scared to speak up. People when they speak about it they speak about it confidentially, quite frankly. People are very worried and nervous about the situation.”
VO:
Dr Munshi’s widow and two daughters requested privacy to mourn their loss, while they continue to pray for justice.
VIZ: HEALTHCARE ACCOUNTABILITY
RINESH: ZOOM: 31:24 - 31:37 (I MOVED THE UPSOUND ABOVE)
“It’s paralysed us, to be honest. It’s paralysed our ability to perform efficiently and appropriately in situations where we need to follow clinical acumen.”
VO:
As the mystery of this unsolved murder deepens, it’s those that took a Hippocratic Oath to help others who say they require protection from society to practice medicine courageously – without having to bear the constant weight of a target on their backs.

__________________________________________________________PROMO 1: CANON CAM 1 – A104C373_2111225G

Was it random? Was it vigilantism? How is it that a top Johannesburg anaesthesiologist was gunned down at this intersection in broad daylight – and nobody knows? the motives behind his murder?

PROMO LINK 2: CANON CAM 1 – A104C373_2111225H (USE AS PROMO)
‘First, do no harm’. That’s the sacred oath that underpins the work that all doctors do. But when things go wrong, they can be held criminally liable – for mistakes many say, leave them traumatised.
NATALIE:
The criminalization prevents the process of learning. It also prevents the process of getting answers – for the family, for the practitioner. It puts it into a win-lose situation, instead of an answering situation. And we want answers.


PROMO 3:
The cold-blooded murder of a prominent Johannesburg doctor has set a precendent of fear among healthcare workers, who claim they’re being targeted and blamed for poor patient outcomes. They’re now questioning: who may be next?
RINESH: ZOOM: 31:24 - 31:37
“It’s paralysed us, to be honest. It’s paralysed our ability to perform efficiently and appropriately in situations where we need to follow clinical acumen.”

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A year after renowned anaesthesiologist Dr Abdulhay Munshi was gunned down, his death continues to raise questions among his family and colleagues.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The shocking daytime murder of a prominent medical specialist sent ripples through the SA medical fraternity last year. And medical practitioners around the country now claim to be living in fear for their own lives.
metadata.Summary: More than a year after Johannesburg anaesthesiologist, Dr Abdulhay Munshi was gunned down in broad daylight in Orange Grove, his family - and the medical fraternity - are still searching for answers. At the time of the killing, a Joburg father who took Munshi and paediatric surgeon Professor Peter Beale to court over the death of his 10-year-old son, Zayyaan Sayed during an operation, denied having a hand in the murder. Mohammadh and Zaheena Sayed had laid charges against Drs Beale and Munshi after the death of their 10-year-old son Zayyaan at the Park Lane Clinic. The Medical Protection Society and the HPCSA have now called for more proactive police investigations into the murder, saying it’s struck fear among surgeons in the province that they too could fall victim to alleged “vigilantism”. The medical fraternity had previously speculated that the culpable homicide case related to the death of Zayyaan and Munshi's shooting could be linked. Munshi’s family, too, are still demanding answers - and closure. They want to know how a prominent doctor’s death has fallen on the wayside of police investigations. *** A look at the status of the investigation a year on, as well as inferences to possible mob involvement, and the psychological effect the murder has had on colleagues within the medical industry.
